must_remember: The Coriolis force is given by the vector expression $F = -2m(\omega \times v)$ in a uniformly rotating frame of reference.
The Coriolis force does zero work on a particle because it is always perpendicular to the velocity vector in the rotating frame.
In the Northern Hemisphere, the Coriolis force deflects moving objects to the right, while in the Southern Hemisphere, the deflection is to the left.
The Coriolis force is zero at the equator and achieves its maximum value at the poles.
A freely falling body dropped from a height experiences an eastward deflection due to the Earth's rotation.
Unlike the centrifugal force which depends on the position vector $r$, the Coriolis force depends on the velocity vector $v$.

glossary.meaning: An inertial or fictitious force experienced by objects in motion within a rotating frame of reference.
An apparent outward force directed radially away from the axis of rotation in a non-inertial rotating frame.
A vector quantity representing the rate of rotation of a coordinate frame, directed along the axis of rotation.
A simple device used to demonstrate the rotation of the Earth, whose plane of oscillation precesses at a rate of $\Omega_p = \omega \sin(\lambda)$.
